author: linkgoron
body:
Clarify the 'close' event description in the child_process docs.

This event is a bit confusing, as the documentation did not state that:

- It's supposed to get emitted after "exit" was already emitted.
- It _also_ emits when the `child_process` has failed to spawn (and thus, `exit` will never be emitted). Another detail, that I did not add to the docs, is that in this case the exit code passed to the closed handler is _negative_. Should this be mentioned?

We were previously checking m_last_error on the miniz struct directly,
which fails to preserve internal invariants and can the leave the reader
broken in specific situations (reading a non-existent file).

Using the provided error checking API fixes this.

This PR includes changes required to run cardano-node v1.26.1.

I've successfully built the Docker image based on this PR.

```
root@3df9d2709ad9:/# cardano-cli --version
cardano-cli 1.26.1 - linux-x86_64 - ghc-8.10
git rev 62f38470098fc65e7de5a4b91e21e36ac30799f3
```

Once the cardano-node starts the DB migration immediately starts as well. Please see the release notes for details https://github.com/input-output-hk/cardano-node/releases/tag/1.26.1

On my local machine the DB migration took about 1.5h with a 3,1 GHz Intel Core i5. I suggest following the steps mentioned in the release notes to mitigate downtime when upgrading live nodes.

author: ralfbrown
body:
Due to the convoluted logic of the existing code, a previous commit to fix a memory leak missed that an item indirectly being freed was still used later in some cases.  Move the later use to be prior to the free, as the only value we actually need from it is an integer.

Presumably due to differences in the memory-allocation code, this error only affected Clang, not GCC.

Fixes #8606.

author: silasbw
body:
### Description

Documentation implies this behavior is intended. For example,
https://docs.celo.org/validator-guide/proxy.

This facilitates running geth without initially configuring a proxy and adding
proxies later via RPCs. For example, like
https://github.com/mantalabs/proxy-informer.

### Tested

Ad hoc testing locally.

### Backwards compatibility

This change is technically a breaking one because it changes the behavior of the
(deprecated) --proxy.proxyenodeurlpair option from required to
optional. This will break uses where --proxy.proxyenodeurlpair is elided and
there's an expectation that geth will fail to start.

Marrowed gemstone will gain stacks from pet and player crits, but does not gain stacks from guardian crits.  Currently simc does not take any pet crits into account for gaining stacks of the buff.

This PR makes several small changes to the core code to allow subscribing to raw order book changes (rather than snapshots) and fixes some bugs in the BetfairAdapters handling of ids.

BetfairAdapter:
 - Fixes `customer_ref` field which is used for de-duping submissions, this now maps to `command.id.value`

Backtests:
- Adds an optional `calculate_data_size` to backtest engine, which caused issues loading some generic data. This is a band-aid fix, more investigation required.

DataClient:
- Add `subscribe_order_book_deltas`

DataEngine: 
- Add `subscribed_order_book_data` & `_handle_subscribe_order_book_deltas`

TradingStrategy:
- Adds `subscribe_order_book_deltas`, `unsubscribe_order_book_deltas` / `handle_order_book_delta` / `on_order_book_delta` to handle new raw orderbook deltas

SocketClient:
- Fixes some bugs in shutdown process 
- Fixes bug partial in recv when we receive partial data

PassiveOrder:
- Adds ability for venue to change its `venue_order_id` on OrderUpdated event
- Adds `_venue_order_ids` to PassiveOrder to track previous venue order ids

Orderbook
- Add safe midpoint function (None if no bid or ask)

author: dholms
body:
## Problem
CORS errors on API requests. Some requests to the gateway (such as `ls`) get forwarded to the API which adds headers to it. So some gateway accessible routes will have CORS errors, even though the gateway as the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` header set.

## Solution
Set the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` header for HTTP API requests as well.

body:
In SDK 41 we are removing the .expo.js extension! We have sent PRs to other repos like [async-storage](https://github.com/react-native-async-storage/async-storage/pull/544) and [react-native-screens](https://github.com/software-mansion/react-native-screens/pull/823) to resolve this, but I only just remembered that we're depending on it here as well. And so this PR was born.

The changes here are backwards compatible, so it doesn't hurt if someone on Expo SDK 39 or 40 installs a version of the library that includes this code. However, when using SDK 41, people will need to use the latest version. To ensure that, I'll add the library to [the list of libraries that we automatically update](https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/87a3673f56cf291c66eebd518801a70115add9be/packages/expo/bundledNativeModules.json) when running `expo upgrade`.

This is me trying to recreate a pattern I often see in `wgpu` examples. The idea is that you have a function that creates all of your required state and stores it in a struct, and then you have another function that renders one specific draw call, whereas your event loop remains in `main.`

This doesn't work with the current system, as you can't really store the necessary `Context???` type or use it in a function because of the `?`s. 

This currently doesn't compile.

Close #335

Refer to a datasheet, it seems that YM2610B has ADPCM-B registers between 0x10 and 0x1C in bank 0, however, YM2608 has the one between 0x00 and 0x10 in bank 1. YM2608 also remove several registers such as `LIMIT ADR` from YM2608.

There is [another difference about a step size](https://github.com/rerrahkr/BambooTracker/issues/335#issuecomment-781149396), I exclude ADPCM-B since it is impossible to convert register values simply.

author: martinpeck
body:
This PR addresses #41 

An additional, optional, parameter to the ApplicationInsights constructor allows the user to control whether the AI logger propagates events to the parent logger.

The default is that is does (i.e. that `propagate_logs` is `True`) to maintain backward compat. By setting this param to `False` the AI events continue to be handled by the `AzureLogHandler`, but are not then propagated to the parent logger and streamed to the console.

If you'd like me to add any examples/update docs, please let me know. 

Happy to help, and thank you for these locust plugins!

author: jdeschamps
body:
Hi there,

Here is the device adapter for a FPGA board that the Ries lab (EMBL) and collaborators have been using for a few years on their microscopes. The platform is called [MicroFPGA](https://github.com/jdeschamps/MicroFPGA) and is based on an hobby FPGA board from Alchitry (Au or Cu, now produced by [SparkFun](https://www.sparkfun.com/categories/tags/alchitry)).

MicroFPGA generats various control signals used on microscopes such as a flexible laser triggering system, servomotors, TTL or PWM (used for instance together with a low-pass for analog output). Together with one of the FPGA board (Au), it can also read in analog signals.

We put some effort in making the [project repository](https://github.com/jdeschamps/MicroFPGA) as documented as possible so that it is easy for people to reproduce and install on their own microscope.

* Brief description of code changes (suitable for use as a commit message):

Do not return error from `iperf_accept()` if it fails to send `ACCESS_DENIED` while running a test.  This is because the new connection request is not related to the running test, and is probably coming from another client or other networking activity (like ports scanning), and returning an error will terminate the active test.

A similar change may be required for the `acccept()` at the beginning of `iperf_accept()` when `test->ctrl_sck != -1`.  I dind't do it because I am not sure if this can happen because a client was able to close the socket before the `accept()` or it means there is a real problem.  Can be added if needed.

author: jfmengels
body:
Propose a fix for removing unused constructors in the `NoUnused.CustomTypeConstructors` rule.

This is only done when the constructor is only used or referenced in the file it was defined in, because `elm-review` doesn't allow multi-file fixes.

What this autofix does:
- Remove the constructor from the custom type
- Remove any pattern match referencing the constructor
- Turn any comparison with expressions referencing the constructor to a boolean
  - `False` for expressions like `if thing == Unused`
  - `True` for expressions like `if thing /= Unused`

![Screenshot from 2021-04-10 12-09-48](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3869412/114266272-afc6a300-99f5-11eb-8406-f452911cbfbd.png)


## Testing

I would like people to test this one out, since there's a higher chance than usual that I messed things up and that it leads to a compiler error.
I'd love it if people could try this one out, and see whether it causes any code to stop compiling or behaving differently.

```bash
npx elm-review --template jfmengels/elm-review-unused/preview#remove-unused-constructor --rules NoUnused.CustomTypeConstructors --fix
```

author: sushidesu
body:
# データベースにおけるNULLの扱い

## やったこと

- [x] 質問に回答 ([回答ファイル](https://github.com/kooooichi24/praha-challenge-pair-1a/blob/task_20_tomoki_ishihara/20/task_20_tomoki_ishihara/task_20_tomoki_ishihara.md))
- [x] クイズの作成

## クイズ

### クイズ1

以下のようなテーブルで、`ORDER BY name` を実行すると、NULLはどのように並び替えられますか？

| id | name |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | a |
| 2 | NULL |
| 3 | b |
| 4 | c |

### クイズ2

`TRUE OR NULL AND NULL` の実行結果はどうなりますか？

### クイズ3

`NOT 100 + 1` の結果はどうなりますか？ (MySQLデフォルトの設定において)

### 参考 (クイズのヒント)

<details>

- クイズ1
  - [MySQL :: MySQL 5.6 リファレンスマニュアル :: 3.3.4.6 NULL 値の操作](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.6/ja/working-with-null.html)
- クイズ2,3
  - [MySQL :: MySQL 5.6 リファレンスマニュアル :: 12.3.3 論理演算子](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.6/ja/logical-operators.html#operator_or)
  - [MySQL :: MySQL 5.6 リファレンスマニュアル :: 12.3.1 演算子の優先順位](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.6/ja/operator-precedence.html)

</details>

author: slike9
body:
Seems `Elem` type member is missed in `ActiveRecord::Relation`. The PR adds it.

The issue is not detected by the tests because of `--suppress-error-code 5002` `sorbet tc` option.

In a real project (in my case) there may be an error:
```
sorbet/rbi/sorbet-typed/lib/activerecord/all/activerecord.rbi:1624: type_member type Enumerable::Elem used outside of the class definition https://srb.help/502
7                                      
    1624 |  sig { params(block: T.nilable(T.proc.params(arg0: Elem).returns(T::Boolean))).returns(T::Boolean) }                                                
```
In my `hidden.rbi`, I have
```ruby
class ActiveRecord::Relation
  include ::Enumerable
  include ::ActiveRecord::Delegation
  ...
end
```

If we add `include Enumerable` into `ActiveRecord::Relation`, the tests will fail with the same errors.

author: ana0
body:
So I started off thinking "Oh I'll just handle the thing where the festival page won't load when you delete a festival-question and make the artworkId not required for festival questions" .... but then I turned up the bug where the festival page displays the wrong question again, when there are multiple questions. I thought we had fixed this one, but I guess not! I feel like it's my fault for not reviewing more thoroughly!

Unfortunately I think that bug might be an unavoidable side-effect of using FestivalHasOneQuestion to represent what is fundamentally a one-to-many relationship, so I added a function to manually find the festival question instead of using the associations (the new function fails if there is no festival-question, or more than one festival-question). Because this isn't using the association anymore, it also breaks inline-question editing. I considered getting that working again, but decided it was probably a lengthy task, that might not be worth it, since there's an edit button below in the table?  I took the route of disabling the Question field on the FestivalEdit view. Questions can still be updated on the QuestionsEdit view. Also glad I looked into this, because question fields weren't being filtered properly when queried via a festival! So this should also be working now :crossed_fingers: 

To test:
1. Create multiple festivals, each with a festival question, and an artwork question
2. Verify that the right question is displayed inline on the festival, and is disabled on the edit page
3. Try deleting and re-creating questions, verify that the FestivalEdit page loads after deleting and also after re-creating

Closes #187

body:
The KIWI API only returns 20 sensors if not given a different page size.
There's no option to return all sensors at the same time.
Passing a suffiently high number to the API call ensures that all the locks are returned.
This fixes problems downstream, where not all locks are visible if a user has many locks in his account to choose from.

body:
<!--
    Hello! Thanks for submitting a pull request to MusicBrainz Picard. We
    appreciate your time and interest in helping our project!

    Use this template to help us review your change. Not everything is required,
    depending on your change. Keep or delete what is relevant for your change.
    Remember that it helps us review if you give more helpful info for us to
    understand your change.

    Ensure that you've read through and followed the Contributing Guidelines, in
    [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/metabrainz/picard/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).
-->

# Summary

<!--
    Update the checkbox with an [x] for the type of contribution you are making.
-->

* This is a…
    * [ ] Bug fix
    * [x] Feature addition
    * [ ] Refactoring
    * [ ] Minor / simple change (like a typo)
    * [ ] Other
* **Describe this change in 1-2 sentences**:

# Problem

<!--
    Anything that helps us understand why you are making this change goes here.
    What problem are you trying to fix? What does this change address?
-->

* JIRA ticket (_optional_): PICARD-2181
* https://github.com/metabrainz/picard-website/pull/229
<!--
    Please make sure you prefix your pull request title with 'PICARD-XXX' in order
    for our ticket tracker to link your pull request to the relevant ticket.
-->

Many plugins try to come with a more comprehensive description, including some markup. So far those plugins contained HTML tags. Allowing markdown will allow easier and better readable (in source) formatting.

# Solution

Use the already used python-markdown module to render the plugin descriptions. As this module is considered optional provide a fallback that only ensures newlines are preserved.

Rendering with Markdown:

![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/29852/114273108-2e810780-9a19-11eb-90a3-a1b45afae336.png)

Without Markdown, using fallback:

![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/29852/114273207-7e5fce80-9a19-11eb-9d1e-794b1a1870bf.png)

As HTML is allowed in markdown existing descriptions continue to render properly. Likewise pure markdown still remains readable without conversion to HTML.

# Action

<!--
    Other than merging your change, do you want / need us to do anything else
    with your change? This could include reviewing a specific part of your PR.
-->

For the listing of downloadable plugins even older Picard versions would render the description fine as the description is served by the website after conversion to HTML. We could change that, but I would keep it that way for compatibility for a while.

We should not immediately start converting plugin descriptions to Markdown, though. Older Picard versions would not render the description of installed plugins properly. Instead we should use Markdown only for plugins compatible with Picard API version 2.7 or later. This change is here to start transitioning.

body:
Bumps [astroid](https://github.com/PyCQA/astroid) from 2.2.3 to 2.5.3.
Release notes

Sourced from astroid's releases.

astroid 2.5

  • Adds attr_fset in the PropertyModel class.

    Fixes PyCQA/pylint#3480

  • Remove support for Python 3.5.

  • Remove the runtime dependency on six. The six brain remains in astroid.

    Fixes PyCQA/astroid#863

  • Enrich the brain_collection module so that __class_getitem__ method is added to deque for python version above 3.9.

  • The context.path is now a dict and the context.push method returns True if the node has been visited a certain amount of times.

    Close #669

  • Adds a brain for type object so that it is possible to write type[int] in annotation.

body:
Original PR: https://github.com/VOREStation/VOREStation/pull/10119
--------------------
Original PR: https://github.com/PolarisSS13/Polaris/pull/8015
--------------------
Initialization on a local test server dropped from ~110s to ~71s
Tested, and lighting and weather still work. I did simplify the logic on umbrellas in the rain, and I commented out the snow/blizzard logic that was _intended_ to make turfs snowy, but which I suspect wasn't working because iterating over all planet turfs every 2 seconds would have generated _enormous_ amounts of lag. I've ideas for a cleaner solution using automata (cave generation).

Removed SSplanets' list of planet turfs/walls because that was completely unused and wasted a huge amount of time and space (~20s initialization different).
Switched planet datum's turf addition/removal to use += after thoroughly tracking the cases where it was triggered (On initializations, on post_change() (Happens through ChangeTurf and similar), and happens when roofing tiles are used on outdoor turfs), added some safeguards to require updates, and added a nice angry comment to warn people off of abusing it.

Planets has to initialize before atoms in order for the planets to exist when the turfs initialize and try to add themselves to those planets, so init order was adjust accordingly.
Sprinkled in a few `as anythings` where the lists as defined could only contain one type, which should hopefully boost runtime performance a little bit as well.

author: vadz
body:
This breaks existing unit tests using wxUIActionSimulator that do things
similar to

	wxUIActionSimulator sim;
	sim.Char('o', wxMOD_CMD);
	wxTEST_DIALOG(wxYield(), ... expected "Open" dialog ...);

because the expected dialog would be shown from inside Char(), unlike
with the wxMSW implementation and GTK until the changes of 59ad9f46e6
(Make wxUIActionSimulator works more reliably on GTK/X11, 2020-05-07).

To still make sure there is a delay after the event, sleep, if
necessary, before simulating the next event: this is still enough for wx
test suite to pass, but allows the code like above to work with both
wxMSW and wxGTK.

In fact, doing it like this makes the code simpler and removes the need
to distinguish between press and release events or maintaining the
number of currently simulated-as-depressed buttons or keys, so it also
simplifies things as a side effect.

Also add some comments and rename Default_Delay constant to a more
accurately named MIN_DELAY_BETWEEN_EVENTS.

---

@AliKet sorry for realising it to late, but the changes of #1845 actually broke some of the UI tests in my own projects with wxGTK because they do things like shown above. AFAICS the version in this PR has mostly the same effect as your changes, while being more compatible with wxMSW and the existing tests, but please let me know if you see anything wrong with it. TIA!

[Issue #12](https://github.com/zmjackson/tides/issues/12)

- [x] Refactored `getFloodLevelData`
   - Pulled logic out to a couple different functions for readability
   - updated how the request is called (i think the correct way now?)
   - added ability for user to select product type
- [x] Created `missing_water_level_dates` json attribute to communicate errors and missing data to front end
- [x] Changed errors in `floods` and `basic_range` so program no longer crashes and just shows empty chart
- [x] Fixed bug where the water levels were actually the sigma values from `data_from_response`

After all the changes, I tried to use as much as I could from `floods` and `basic_range`, but in the end I don't actually use these functions within the `getFloodLevelData`. Due to the fact that we want to allow the user to access more than 31 days at a time, we can't just go through a numpy array adding all the values that are over the threshold. There also needs to be some breaks in the array to record the start and end dates to provide information for the duration of the flood. 

Hopefully this looks a little cleaner, and all the functionality should be there. 

Github makes the file comparison looks like trash, so if you take a look at it I would just view it as a single file.

author: bmangoen
body:
# Changes

## Adding Dockerfile.rhel

Just add the [Dockerfile.rhel](https://github.com/projectcalico/atomic-wireguard/blob/master/Dockerfile.rhel) to this repository for not having a dependency to the [atomic-wireguard git repository](https://github.com/projectcalico/atomic-wireguard).

## WireGuard kmod configuration

`KMOD_CONTAINER_BUILD_CONTEXT` into the [wireguard-kmod.conf](https://github.com/tigera/kvc-wireguard-kmod/blob/master/wireguard-kmod.conf#L4) can now be set to this current repository.

`WIREGUARD_KERNEL_VERSION` into the [wireguard-kmod.conf](https://github.com/tigera/kvc-wireguard-kmod/blob/master/wireguard-kmod.conf#L10) should not be hardcoded and could be dynamically set the host kernel version.

## Removing sanity checks for the wireguard-kmod build

As the variable `WIREGUARD_KERNEL_VERSION` could be set dynamically, there is no need to do [sanity checks](https://github.com/tigera/kvc-wireguard-kmod/blob/master/wireguard-kmod-lib.sh#L100-L119) if the built kmods are built against the correct module software version.

Moreover, there is an issue of *endless loop* for this build_kmods because there is the following [check](https://github.com/tigera/kvc-wireguard-kmod/blob/master/wireguard-kmod-lib.sh#L107-L110) which always fails and is re-executed [build_kmod_container](https://github.com/tigera/kvc-wireguard-kmod/blob/master/wireguard-kmod-lib.sh#L109) due to the wrong path:

```shell
...
STEP 26: COMMIT wireguard-kmod-v1.0:4.18.0-193.29.1.el8_2.x86_64
--> 702ec817098
[Warning] one or more build args were not consumed: [KMODVER KVER]                                                                                                                             
702ec81709841a33873e8c24597f64f1cd42ffb0433b02ca1a8f9ee51c0d1d11
Checking for old kernel module images that need to be recycled                                                                                                                                 
++ podman images -q -f label=name=wireguard-kmod -f dangling=true
++ podman images -q -f label=name=wireguard-kmod -f dangling=false
Cleaning up old kernel module container builds
+ podman rmi -f 32e1b1dcaa0b
21e29e5a4568bf16502f12c44e86a810ad6844f6a44d413dd08ef5990e7f8451
Deleted: 32e1b1dcaa0b778d511f2981eefbcc8a44a5cae3a97fe7a6e2c65829e002bdd8
++ podman run -i --rm wireguard-kmod-v1.0:4.18.0-193.29.1.el8_2.x86_64 modinfo -F version /lib/modules/4.18.0-193.29.1.el8_2.x86_64/udp-tunnel.ko
modinfo: ERROR: Module /lib/modules/4.18.0-193.29.1.el8_2.x86_64/udp-tunnel.ko not found.
Module version mismatch within container. rebuilding wireguard-kmod-v1.0:4.18.0-193.29.1.el8_2.x86_64
Building wireguard-kmod-v1.0:4.18.0-193.29.1.el8_2.x86_64 kernel module container...
...
```

# Test

## Prerequisites

- All needed RPMs are stored in a HTTP server

Tested on:

- OpenShift Container Platform 4.6.8
  - Red Hat CoreOS nodes with kernel version *4.18.0-193.29.1.el8_2.x86_64*
  - Using WireGuard version *1.0.20200520*
- OpenShift Container Platform 4.7.4
  - RHCOS nodes with kernel version *4.18.0-240.15.1.el8_3.x86_64*
  - Using WireGuard version *1.0.20210219*

## Example of configuration file

- `wireguard-kmod.conf` file:

```shell
# The configuration file for the simple-kmod kernel module
# softare bundle that is to be used with the kmods-via-containers
# framework.
KMOD_CONTAINER_BUILD_CONTEXT="git://github.com/bmangoen/kvc-wireguard-kmod"
KMOD_CONTAINER_BUILD_FILE=Dockerfile.rhel
KMOD_SOFTWARE_VERSION=v1.0
KMOD_NAMES="udp_tunnel ip6_udp_tunnel wireguard"
KMOD_EXTRA_NAMES="udp_tunnel ip6_udp_tunnel"
WIREGUARD_PRUNE_OLD_VERSIONS=false
WIREGUARD_KERNEL_VERSION=$(uname -r)
WIREGUARD_SHA256=99d35296b8d847a0d4db97a4dda96b464311a6354e75fe0bef6e7c4578690f00
WIREGUARD_VERSION=1.0.20210219
KERNEL_CORE_RPM=http://x.x.x.x:8080/kernel-core-$(uname -r).rpm
KERNEL_DEVEL_RPM=http://x.x.x.x:8080/kernel-devel-$(uname -r).rpm
KERNEL_MODULES_RPM=http://x.x.x.x:8080/kernel-modules-$(uname -r).rpm
```

author: amoodie
body:
Previously we did not support specifying any other options along with the "set" specification in the preprocessor.

This PR implements ensemble support for set specification. This is achieved similarly to ensemble expansion for a matrix, where separate seeds are specified for each case. Here, however, we simply create a N copies of each set item, where `ensemble: N`, and a separate seed is specified for each replicate of each set.

Adds simple test to cover this case.

### Description:

Changed the drop rate of Lil Lamb to bring it in line with the other BSO pets and the =petrates command.
(Currently the drop rate for Lil Lamb is actually 1 in 2666.67 hours at BEST. You get 1 roll at 8k rate PER TRIP > 20 minutes).

### Changes:

Instead of getting only 1 roll at a 1 in 8k per minimum 20 minute trip, this divides 8000 by the number of minutes (including fractional) and then gives the modified roll. 

This fixes the drop rate to be 1 in 8000 minutes, instead of 1 in 8000x 20+ minute trips (min. of 2666.67 hours)

I have tested the code, it seems to properly divide the drop rate as it should.

body:
### Summary <!-- Required -->

This pull request adds the linguistics major and minor to CoursePlan

Major
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25535093/114282843-59b52800-9a14-11eb-8816-1083bbbe8585.png)

Minor
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25535093/114283967-c03d4480-9a1a-11eb-8e05-a858bfa8d0e1.png)

### Test Plan <!-- Required -->

1. Confirm the checkers match the information here: https://linguistics.cornell.edu/undergraduate
2. More specifically, add the core classes and confirm they cannot fulfill other linguistics requirements
3. Confirm that additional courses logic holds up (split similarly to liberal studies, has a double countable credit req)
4. Confirm any course can be added to the ancillary skills courses (outside the core courses).
5. Confirm these requirements work for the minor as well.
5. Check that all the text makes sense and is typo-free, and that the urls link where they should

### Notes <!-- Optional -->

Ran into a few issues when creating this major and minor, and was wondering if we currently have any way of handling these.
- Is there any way we can restrict courses to only display ones that are 3 (or more) credits? Right now I have an 18 credit checker for the additional courses, which is not technically correct, as 2 credit courses could be used to fulfill this requirement when they can't in reality.
- Do we have any way to check a course does not have the "CU-UGR" designation? It shows up in student center under "Course Attribute": https://classes.cornell.edu/browse/roster/FA20/class/LING/4491
- Is there any way to check the restriction that "language courses" cannot be used for additional courses? I don't think so because LING courses can be crosslisted with language course codes and not count as a "language course," but still unsure.
- Right now, one course can be used to fulfill the 3000, 2000, and 1000 course for the minor  but not the major, I think because of the way double counting works (even though none of the requirements are set to allow double counting). Should I rework this requirement for the minor and make it different than the major?

author: maxeckel
body:
This PR resolves issue #99 and is based on the PR by @ahmedash95 #144.

The PR resolves the issue of being able to use directory traversal in conjunction with symlinks mentioned by @taylorotwell in #144.

In order to prevent the directory traversal, I take the path following the symlink and check whether the resolved path using realpath() ends with the requested path.

**For example:**

Requested URL: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/storage/../../../.env`

realpath() output: `/my/project/directory/.env`

Since `storage` is the symlink, the path `../../../.env` will be checked against the realpath() output. 
Because of the traversal attempt, the paths don't match and the request won't be served statically.

body:
I'm trying to use composer2nix with a PHP 8.0-only project, and, well, it (specifically composer) doesn't work unless it's run under PHP 8.0, which is not currently the default `php` attribute in `nixos-unstable`.

I currently import composer2nix in a dev shell like so: https://github.com/jbboehr/php-psr/blob/d9003822a540fc35627d63baa48445ed81742fd1/default.nix#L20

A composer update is required as some older versions of packages did not list PHP 8.0 as supported.

## About The Pull Request

Part 2 of ~~5~~ however many it takes.

This tunes the reactions to the new mechanics in the same way as before. The recipe specific reactions Here's the changes!
_Feel free to suggest better names for the impure chems_

## Reagents

### Manitol

#### Reagent changes

Scales healing with purity
Default purity is 0.75
Adds an OD that does no damage, but makes you feel enlightened (gives you cool tips!)

#### Impure effects

Gives the user a random speech impediment that is removed when the impurity reagent is removed

### Neurine

#### Reagent changes

When added to a patient, it will remember their brain damage - if their brain damage is below that value when added it will restore it back to what it was on consumption
When used on the dead will heal a corpse's brain slowly
Scales healing with purity
Default purity is 0.75

#### Impure and inverse effects

Gives the user a random brain trauma that is removed when the impurity reagent is removed.

### Ephedrine

#### Reagent changes

Scales effects with purity
Default purity is 0.75
Reaction is now dangerous - (will explode on overheat/overly impure!)

#### Inverse effects

Stops the patients heart - forcing them to beat it manually while it's in their system (aka temporary cursed heart)

### Antihol

#### Reagent changes

Scales effects with purity
Default purity is 0.75

#### Inverse effects

Increases the booze power of all alcohols in a patient (use it to spike alcoholic drinks!). 

### Oculine

#### Reagent changes

Scales effects with purity
Default purity is 0.75
Improves your ability to see in the dark base off purity while it's in your system

#### Inverse effects

Has a chance to induce a temporary ocular migraine - blinding you.

### Inacusiate

#### Reagent changes

Scales effects with purity
Default purity is 0.75
Lets you hear whispers from a distance if it's 100% pure

#### Impure effects

Screws with your hearing - making people's messages appear funny (changes hear messages' spans)

## Other things

I improved the chem reaction debug machine for other people to use, so they can easily edit their reaction vars in game while testing it.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33956696/111675221-cb82c300-8814-11eb-8369-cf1e116b9b4c.png)

Partially refactors how explosions are handled - but I plan to go into this in a lot more depth when I get around to touching explosives.

Adds a few chemistry tips!

## Why It's Good For The Game

Continuing the adjustments of the older chems to be in line with the new mechanics while increasing the amount of impure chems for people to play with!

balance: Adjusts Mannitol,Neurine,Ephephrine,Prohol,Oculine and Inacusate to have their own reaction profiles, purity and impurity effects
qol: Improves the debug reaction tester so that reaction vars can be live edited to make reaction tweaking/creation less of a pain.

author: kirillosenkov
body:
It would be very useful to embed more than just the project files into the binlog. For example, project.assets.json is a common request: https://github.com/dotnet/msbuild/issues/3529. global.json or nuget.config would be other examples. Some users may want to embed all *.cs files as well.

Add a special EmbedInBinlog item type recognized by BuildEventArgsWriter. If after evaluation the items contain EmbedInBinlog, all such items will be logged if the evaluated include points to a full file path that exists on disk. A given file can be mentioned more than once, but will only be embedded once. If a file doesn't exist or is empty, it will not be embedded. If the item is added from a target (after evaluation is done), it will not be embedded.

Checking for EmbedInBinlog is done in BuildEventArgsWriter to reuse the complicated and performance-optimized logic of iterating over all items.

This PR is a prerequisite for https://github.com/dotnet/msbuild/issues/3529
